The Reactor Pilot Program, DOME test bed, and Nuclear Energy Launch Pad put four DOE-authorized criticalities on the board by July 4, 2026, the authorization channel first units are using.
Selected Idaho National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Paducah, and Savannah River in December 2025 to host AI data centers paired with new generation, including co-located advanced reactors.
UPRISE targets 2.5 GW of added capacity by 2027 and 5 GW by 2029 through uprates, license renewals, and restarts of the existing fleet.

The $350M Texas Advanced Nuclear Development Fund opened in April 2026 through two reimbursement programs, one for advanced nuclear construction and one for project design and supply chain work.

Great British Energy - Nuclear selected Rolls-Royce SMR as its preferred technology partner in June 2025 and signed the development contract, with £2.6B allocated in the 2025 Spending Review to enable it.
Sizewell C reached its final investment decision in July 2025 under the first nuclear regulated-asset-base structure, around £38B, with the UK government the largest shareholder.
GE Vernova Hitachi and Orlen Synthos Green Energy signed the Poland Generic Design Agreement in Washington on February 24, 2026, advancing the Polish generic design of the BWRX-300.
Poland's first SMR will be constructed at Włocławek, one of six locations OSGE shortlisted in 2023 for geological surveys to host BWRX-300 plants.
Industrial partners in Poland and the UK hold 34 executed Last Energy PPAs totaling 680 MW, roughly $18.9B in power sales.
Ontario approved OPG's four-unit Darlington BWRX-300 program at C$20.9B in 2024 dollars, C$7.7B of it for the first unit and shared systems.
The Saskatchewan Research Council is the first announced commercial eVinci customer, planning a pilot by 2029.
RoPower took the final investment decision for a 462 MWe six-module NuScale plant at Doicești.
The U.S.-Japan investment framework earmarks up to $40B for BWRX-300 builds at unidentified Tennessee and Alabama sites; a strategic framework, not a construction contract.

Meralco PowerGen and Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation signed a cooperation agreement, witnessed by President Marcos, for a pre-feasibility study of USNC's 15 MWe Micro-Modular Reactor; Meralco holds an option to pursue a full feasibility study on the results.

The U.S. Trade and Development Agency committed $2.7M to Meralco PowerGen for a technical review of U.S. SMR designs and an implementation roadmap, under the U.S.-Philippines 123 Agreement (effective July 2024) and toward the Philippines' stated goal of 1,200 MW of nuclear capacity online by 2032.

SK Innovation and TerraPower signed a term sheet to advance Korea's first commercial Natrium plant under a domestic 'K-Sodium' business model, alongside Hyundai Engineering & Construction as EPC contractor for up to eight Natrium reactors, HD Hyundai as manufacturing partner, and Export-Import Bank of Korea financing; no financial terms disclosed.

Nano Nuclear Energy and DS Dansuk signed a non-binding, non-exclusive MOU for DS Dansuk to serve as local coordinator (siting, supply chain, regulatory) for Nano's KRONOS Micro Modular Reactor under Korea's 'One Factory, One MMR' strategy.

Vattenfall narrowed its Värö Peninsula new-build competition (about 1,500 MW) from 75 initial suppliers to two finalists, GE Vernova (five BWRX-300 units) and Rolls-Royce SMR (three units); the process continues toward a final supplier.

GE Vernova Hitachi and Fortum signed an early-works agreement for pre-licensing and site-adaptation engineering on the BWRX-300 in both Finland and Sweden, with potential deployment in the second half of the 2030s, after Fortum's own feasibility study selected the design as a candidate for both countries.

Norsk Kjernekraft and Aecon (Canada's contractor on Darlington's BWRX-300) entered a strategic cooperation covering feasibility studies, licensing, stakeholder engagement, and site identification for the BWRX-300 across ten locations Norsk Kjernekraft has identified for environmental assessment.

Altra (operator of the shut-down Ignalina plant), Poland's SGE, and GE Vernova Hitachi signed an MOU in Washington, with Lithuania's energy minister and two DOE deputy assistant secretaries present, to assess the technical and economic feasibility of BWRX-300 deployment in Lithuania.

USTDA and state-owned Bulgarian Energy Holding agreed to a detailed technical prefeasibility study of US-sourced SMR design options, potential sites, and an implementation roadmap including financing, building on a 2021 Fluor-NuScale MOU that did not advance.

Westinghouse and state-owned JAVYS signed MOUs framing collaboration on both the AP1000 large reactor and the AP300 small modular reactor for Slovakia; Westinghouse targets AP300 design certification by 2027 and a first unit operating in 2033.

Nuclear Power Ghana and Regnum Technology Group agreed to deploy a NuScale VOYGR-12 plant, planned as Africa's first commercial advanced light-water SMR, with a subsidiary company to own and operate it.

The World Bank Group formalized an IAEA partnership in June 2025, its first concrete step to reengage with nuclear power in decades, covering life extension of existing plants and SMR development for developing countries.
A statewide push to replace rural diesel generation with microreactors, with a stated goal of all Alaskans having access to 10-cent power by 2030 and state microreactor siting law in place.

DOE's Idaho National Laboratory funded and reviewed a preliminary feasibility study by the Nuclear Alternative Project, concluding SMRs and microreactors could supply zero-emission, hurricane-resilient baseload power cost-competitive with the mobile gas units and combined-cycle turbines PREPA proposed for its fleet replacement.

Proyecto de la Cámara 1092, which would amend Puerto Rico's energy policy act to direct government evaluation of SMR deployment, drew supporting testimony from the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau's president and an ANS student chapter at a House Economic Development Commission hearing; the bill had not passed as of the hearing.

The full Puerto Rico House of Representatives passed C.P. 1092, advancing it to the Senate; the bill keeps the island's 100%-renewable-by-2050 goal but permits evaluating nuclear as a low-emission complementary technology under NRC supervision, and directs the University of Puerto Rico to build nuclear-engineering academic programs. Still a bill, not law: no funded program exists until the Senate and governor act.

Guam senators say DOD has set aside roughly $400M for small reactors at two Guam installations, a figure attributed to Sen. Telo Taitague; Guam's Community Defense Liaison Office says the territory's government has received no official DOD notification or confirmed plan.

The FY2026 NDAA, signed into law December 2025, requires the Secretary of Defense to give Congress and Guam's governor at least one year's notice before placing any nuclear reactor on the island, a provision credited to Del. James Moylan; a procedural notice requirement, not evidence DOD has a site or plan.
DOE's UPRISE initiative targets 2.5 GW of added capacity by 2027 and 5 GW by 2029 through uprates and restarts, the same near-term channel the three executed hyperscaler PPAs bought into.
Transferable 45Y/48E tax credits cover a large share of capital for reactors beginning construction by 2034, and nuclear survived the 2025 phase-outs that hit wind and solar.
